findings.title: Element-loop guard is defined three times with conflicting rules
findings.description: `ELEMENT_LOOP_NODES` appears in three test modules with different contents. `test_import_boundary.py:172-180` includes `ast.GeneratorExp`, and its own test (around line 199) requires `sum(x for x in y)` to be detected. `test_labels.py:27` and `test_confidence.py:25` omit `GeneratorExp`, with a comment saying generator expressions are allowed. The exemption was sanctioned for `labels.py`'s `all(...)` over category ids (`project-documents/user/tasks/105-tasks.labels-signals-and-declarations.md:167`). The copies apply it to every module they guard. `confidence.py` contains no generator, so its guard (`test_confidence.py:133-135`) allows a pattern it never needs, and a per-element `all(v for v in values)` would pass unnoticed. The 104 review (`project-documents/user/reviews/archive/104-review.code.series-and-point-series.20261110T153732.md:193`) fixed this same gap and required generator expressions to be detected. Fix: keep one shared guard with an explicit allowance for the category-id check, and drop the exemption from `confidence.py`.

findings.title: Module docstring overstates "no element loops" in labels.py
findings.description: The docstring says "there are no element loops". `labels.py:64-66` runs `all(... for category in self.category_ids)`. That check runs over the category-id set, not an array, and the design allows it, so the code is correct. The docstring should say "no element loops over arrays" or mention that one `all(...)`.

findings.title: `LABELS_SIGNALS_DECLARATIONS_MODULES` names modules it does not describe
findings.description: The list includes `value_checks.py`, `confidence.py` and `display.py`. The name implies only labels, signals and declarations. It is used at lines 50, 143 and 160. Rename it to something like `SLICE_105_MODULES`, or split it.

findings.title: `InvalidParametersError` breaks the `CoreModelError(message)` constructor contract
findings.description: `__init__(self, issues)` takes a tuple. Every other `CoreModelError` takes a message, and the helpers in `validation.py` and `value_checks.py` call `error(message)` on an `error: type[CoreModelError]`. If this class were ever passed as that factory, `InvalidParametersError("msg")` would construct silently with `issues == "msg"`. `str()` would then raise `AttributeError`, because `__str__` iterates the string's characters. No current caller does this; `Declarations.bind_parameters` is the only raise site. A type check in `__init__` would make the trap fail at construction.

findings.title: One parametrized test exercises no production code
findings.description: `test_match_selects_the_branch_for_each_form` builds the output dataclasses and runs a `match` written inside the test body. It checks that the classes expose `name`, which is the only thing it verifies. Nothing in `declarations.py` decides the branch. Delete it, or keep only the attribute check, and label it as such.

findings.title: Fixture types are weakened to `Any` in test_labels.py
findings.description: `make_bar_index: Any` also appears at line 233. Other test modules declare a local `MakeBarIndex` alias (`test_series_index.py:33`), and `conftest.py:59` defines the same type. Use that alias. Strict pyright accepts explicit `Any`, so this is weak typing, not a type error.

findings.title: Numeric coercion has a single path
findings.description: `as_integer` and `as_real` are the only numeric coercions. `confidence.py`, `signals.py` and `declarations.py` reach them through `require_real` or `_coerce`, and none defines its own. `as_real` catches only `OverflowError`, with a justifying comment. `10**400`, `2**63`, `True`, `Decimal` and NaN/inf all return `None`. `canonical.py:122-123` normalizes `-0.0` to `0.0`, so a bound `-0.0` canonicalizes the same as its default.

findings.title: Parameter binding keeps order and collects every issue
findings.description: Declared parameters come first in declared order, then unknown names sorted. Every issue is collected before `InvalidParametersError` is raised. The returned `MappingProxyType` is read-only. `canonical.py:233` accepts any `Mapping`, so an omitted default and an explicit equal value canonicalize to the same bytes. Copy and pickle round-trips are covered by `test_declarations.py`.
